text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (9.8%, 2,395, 1.8%, 10.60, z 0.80, 69%, 45 records, 19 documented 99215s with 0 below billed, 2 of 34). Language is cautious and the leaning is inconclusive, and next steps are reasonable. However, the rationale has internal contradictions and cites claims that don't support the sentences using them: C0000189, C0000222, C0000251 are not on the card, the 'time-repeat signal' is not in the evidence, and the note-sign percentages come from tool output that can't be verified here. It says 'the billing pattern points toward upcoding' while leaning inconclusive. The 'elevated in every stratum' claim is only loosely supported, and the z-score of 0.80 undermines the 'far above' headline. C0001996 is cited as a one-condition patient documented high, which is supported. Overall it is usable but muddled, so an investigator would need to redo some of the analysis.","problems":["Cites C0000189, C0000222, C0000251 as examples of the problems signal; these are not on the evidence card, so support cannot be verified","Mentions a 'time-repeat signal on some' notes with no figure or support in the evidence","Says 'billing pattern points toward upcoding' while leaning is inconclusive and the later text hedges; inconsistent tone","Headline 'far above' expectation sits awkwardly with a peer z-score of 0.80, and the discrepancy is not explained","Sample 'back pain, abdominal pain, UTI or follow-up' examples are fine, but C0000713 (Z09) is described as follow-up only loosely","Speculation that notes are written to match billed level is weakly supported by a 60% problems signal and 2 of 34 data-without-lab","Next step suggests examining 'flagged problem-list notes' without identifying them; the targeted chart request is partly redundant since 45 charts are already returned and none was below billed level"]}
